notes: an ScVal bool encoded as 2. RFC 4506 defines bool as an enum of FALSE = 0 and TRUE = 1, but neither reference rejects it: xdrpp, which core uses, maps any non-zero value to TRUE (xdr_traits<bool>::from_uint is u != 0, so validate_enum sees true), while stellar-xdr maps anything but 1 to false. the same bytes are therefore true to core and false to rust consumers, and no conforming encoder writes them. a decoder should refuse them; the entry is implementation-defined because the references do not. stellar-xdr 30.0.0 decodes it but does not round-trip (re-encoded bytes differ: 8 bytes in, 8 out, first difference at byte 7) under Limits { depth: 1000 (xdr.envelope.depth), len: 8 }.
